patches.value: For t>0, E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t) dx. This finite Lebesgue integral is used only once integrability of e(·,t) at every positive time has been proved; no definition at time zero is required.

C⊆int Q, and Q is compact and measurable with finite Lebesgue measure (2R)^n. For every r∈int J, the spatial functions e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t(·,r)·u_tt(·,r), and, for every j∈{1,…,n}, u_j(j,·,r)·v_j(j,·,r), u_t(·,r)·u_jj(j,·,r), u_t(·,r)·u_j(j,·,r), and ∂_{x_j}(u_t(·,r)·u_j(j,·,r)) are continuous and vanish outside C. Their nonzero sets therefore have closures contained in the compact set C.
